title: Report each wagon's coupling complexity and flag those above the soft threshold

facts.note: The reporter runs on every planner validation, for every wagon in the plan, whether or not anything changed.
Assumed file kinds (not source-backed scope); used as hints, not an exclusive filter. Threshold changes in configuration alone can create or clear flags.

values: wagon produce/consume artifact name added, removed or renamed
facts.note: Diff observer on produce/consume names and the config key; file matching alone does not establish a graph change. Not required for firing: unchanged plans are still reported.
Emitted by `atdd validate planner` when a wagon's fan_in x fan_out exceeds the configured threshold.

fires: `atdd validate planner` runs on any plan, including an unchanged existing plan: every wagon's fan_in x fan_out is reported.
A planner adds a consume entry that raises a wagon's fan_in x fan_out above the threshold (default 6): reported and flagged advisory.
Only planner.wagon.coupling_complexity_threshold is changed in configuration: all wagons re-reported and flags recomputed against the new cutoff.
A wagon's product is at or below the threshold: still reported, but no advisory flag (no-advisory case, reporting still fires).
doesNotFire: Work that involves no plan/wagon graph and no planner validation (e.g. editing application code outside planning).
Deciding whether to block or halt planning: this rule never fires as a blocker.

given: A plan whose wagons declare produce/consume artifacts, forming a directed wagon graph keyed on artifact NAMES.
when: You plan or validate the plan (`atdd validate planner`), including unchanged plans and threshold-only config changes.
then: Report every wagon's coupling complexity (fan_in x fan_out over the produce->consume name graph) and flag, as advisory and non-blocking, each wagon above the soft threshold planner.wagon.coupling_complexity_threshold (default 6).
prefer: Run `atdd validate planner` so each wagon's complexity is visible while planning.
fan_in = wagons consumed from; fan_out = wagons consuming its outputs; reason on the product (Henry-Kafura).
avoid: Blocking or halting planning on the advisory.
Keying coupling on the nullable contract field instead of artifact names.
Renaming/merging artifact names only to lower the product.
why: High fan_in x fan_out marks an entangled wagon that hurts separability; non-blocking reporting keeps complexity visible until the threshold is calibrated.
evidence: `atdd validate planner` output reports coupling complexity for every wagon, with advisory findings only for wagons whose fan_in x fan_out strictly exceeds the configured threshold.
Validator exit status is unaffected by coupling-complexity findings (advisory, severity 2).
verifier_detail: Build the directed wagon graph from produce->consume artifact NAMES (not the nullable contract field).
fan_in = number of distinct wagons a wagon consumes from; fan_out = number of distinct wagons that consume its outputs; proxy = fan_in x fan_out (Henry-Kafura).
Report the proxy for each wagon; emit an ADVISORY finding when proxy > threshold (strictly exceeds); threshold from config key planner.wagon.coupling_complexity_threshold, default 6.
Non-blocking: advisory only, never blocks or fails the run; disposition advisory, severity 2.
Promotion to a hard threshold / strict disposition is deferred to corpus calibration.

Terms: coupling_complexity = fan_in x fan_out over the cross-wagon produce/consume graph (Henry-Kafura proxy); soft_threshold = config-driven advisory cutoff (planner.wagon.coupling_complexity_threshold, default 6), over it emits an advisory finding.
